question: How much do larger and better-filtered pre-training data plus staged SFT, DPO and GRPO improve an open-weight LLM family over Qwen2?
hypothesis: Scaling and mixing data (7T to 18T tokens) and multistage post-training improve capability across sizes.
contributions: Open-weight 0.5B-72B base and instruct models plus MoE Turbo and Plus
1M-token context for Turbo via progressive extension, YARN, DCA, sparse attention

method.summary: Technical report for the Qwen2.5 family: dense decoder transformers 0.5B-72B (open) and two MoE API models, pretrained on 18T tokens, then SFT, DPO and GRPO. Evaluated on open and in-house benchmarks against Llama 3/3.1, Gemma2, Mistral and GPT-4o variants. No ablations and no pre-training hyperparameter values.

datasets.name: Qwen2.5 pre-training corpus
datasets.source: Proprietary; includes Qwen2.5-Math and Qwen2.5-Coder data and synthetic data from Qwen2-72B-Instruct and Qwen2-Math-72B-Instruct
datasets.preprocessing: Qwen2-Instruct models score and filter; domain down/up-sampling; n-gram decontamination (LCS>=13 and >=0.6 x min length)

datasets.name: SFT data
datasets.source: Proprietary: long-response, math CoT, code, instruction-following, structured data, 70,000 logical reasoning queries, cross-lingual, system prompts
datasets.preprocessing: Rejection sampling, execution feedback, critic and multi-agent filtering

datasets.name: Offline RL (DPO) pairs
datasets.source: Resampled from SFT model; pass/fail on quality checks

datasets.name: Open benchmarks and in-house English/Chinese sets
datasets.source: MMLU, MMLU-Pro, GSM8K, MATH, HumanEval, MBPP, IFEval, Arena-Hard, MT-Bench, RULER, LV-Eval and others

models.name: Qwen2.5 dense 0.5B/1.5B/3B/7B/14B/32B/72B
models.architecture: decoder-only Transformer with GQA, SwiGLU, RoPE, QKV bias, RMSNorm pre-norm

other.tie_embedding: Yes for 0.5B,1.5B,3B; No for 7B and up

models.name: Qwen2.5-Turbo / Qwen2.5-Plus
models.architecture: MoE: fine-grained expert segmentation, shared experts, top-K routing

other.note: expert counts and parameters not stated

training.objective: Pre-training: not stated explicitly (next-token implied); SFT; DPO; GRPO
training.optimizer: Online Merging Optimizer for DPO; pre-training optimizer not stated
training.lr: SFT 7e-6 to 7e-7; DPO 7e-7; pre-training lr from scaling law, value not stated
training.batch_size: GRPO 2048 global; pre-training from scaling law, not stated

other.scaling_law_study: dense 44M-14B and MoE 44M-1B activated params, 0.8B-600B tokens, used to predict optimal lr and batch size
other.turbo_long_ctx_mix: 40% sequences at current max length, 60% shorter

inference.prompting: Base: MMLU 5-shot, BBH 3-shot, ARC-C 25-shot, HellaSwag 10-shot, GSM8K/MATH 4-shot, coding 0-shot

parameters.long_context: YARN and Dual Chunk Attention give four-fold length capacity: 1M for Turbo, 131,072 for others

metrics.name: Benchmark accuracy / pass rates
metrics.definition: per benchmark, as in open suites

eval.protocol: Single reported scores, no seeds or confidence intervals; baseline numbers partly from other reports (not stated which)

availability.weights: Hugging Face, ModelScope, Kaggle; 3B and 72B under custom licences

results.claim: Pre-training data was scaled from 7T to 18T tokens.
results.setup: Qwen2.5 dense and MoE models vs Qwen2
results.quote:
we have scaled the high-quality pre-training datasets from the
previous 7 trillion tokens to 18 trillion tokens

results.claim: Qwen2.5-72B base scores 86.1 MMLU (5-shot), above Qwen2-72B 84.2 and Llama-3-405B 85.2.
Qwen2.5-7B base: 74.2 MMLU, 49.8 MATH, 57.9 HumanEval, with 6.5B non-embedding parameters.
results.quote:
achieving 74.2 on general benchmarks like MMLU (Hendrycks et al., 2021a), 49.8 on math
challenges such as MATH (Hendrycks et al., 2021b), and 57.9 on coding tasks like HumanEval
the non-embedding parameters of Qwen2-7B and Qwen2.5-7B are only 6.5B

results.claim: Qwen2.5-Turbo reaches 100% passkey retrieval at 1M tokens.
results.quote:
Qwen2.5-Turbo achieves 100% accuracy in the 1M-token passkey
retrieval task

results.claim: Sparse attention cuts attention compute 12.5x at 1M tokens; TTFT speedup 3.2 to 4.3x.
results.quote:
this approach reduces the computational load of the attention mechanism by
12.5 times

results.claim: RULER average for Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct is 95.1 with DCA+YARN versus 90.8 without; at 128K it is 88.4 vs 67.0.
results.table: Table 16, row Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct and w/o DCA + YARN, columns Avg. and 128K

results.claim: Context extension: 4,096 to 32,768 tokens in final pre-training stage with RoPE base 10,000 to 1,000,000 (ABF).
results.quote:
we extend the context length from 4,096 to 32,768 tokens during the final
pre-training stage for all model variants except Qwen2.5-Turbo. Concurrently, we increase the base
frequency of RoPEfrom 10,000 to 1,000,000 using the ABF technique

results.claim: SFT: over 1M examples, 2 epochs, seq len 32,768, lr 7e-6 to 7e-7, weight decay 0.1, grad clip 1.0.
results.quote:
The model is fine-tuned for two epochs
with a sequence length of 32,768 tokens. To optimize learning, the learning rate is gradually decreased
from 7 × 10−6 to 7 × 10−7.

results.claim: Offline RL: about 150,000 DPO pairs, one epoch, lr 7e-7.
results.quote:
we
construct a dataset consisting of approximately 150,000 training pairs. The model is then trained for one
epoch using the Online Merging Optimizer (Lu et al., 2024a), with a learning rate of 7 × 10−7.

results.claim: Online RL GRPO: 8 responses per query, global batch 2048.
results.quote:
We sample 8 responses
for each query. All models are trained with a 2048 global batch size

results.claim: Qwen2.5-RM-72B Reward Bench score 91.59, below Llama-3.1-Nemotron-70B-Reward 94.10; best on PPE objective-avg 69.85.
Contamination filter: remove a training sequence if LCS with a test sequence is at least 13 tokens and at least 0.6 of the shorter length.
results.setup: n-gram decontamination on pre- and post-training data

results.claim: Open-weight table: 0.5B/1.5B/3B tie embeddings, 7B and up do not; layers 24/28/36/28/48/64/80; GQA KV heads 2/2/2/4/8/8/8.
results.table: Table 1, column Tie Embedding and Layers

limits: No ablations isolating the effect of data size, filtering or each post-training stage.
Pre-training hyperparameters (lr, batch size, optimizer), hardware and compute are not given; the scaling-law results are described without numbers.
MoE sizes and expert counts of Turbo and Plus not stated.
Authors concede reward-model benchmark scores do not predict RL model quality, and cultural nuance (BLEnD) needs more work.
Per-size token counts are not stated; the abstract gives 18T for the series.
